beats.narration_text: Sawubona, Liam. Today: session. One skill, two pastes: a STYLE box and direction-tagged lyrics. Suno knows how to sing — it never knew how to read. Session notes fix that. Liam, in for Bear.

beats.narration_text: Session has two paths. Path A — automated: art suno reads a beat_sheet and emits the style box, direction-tagged lyrics, and a beat map; the human pastes into Suno, generates, and the stem drops into pantry. Path B — authored: for poems, the human writes the STYLE box and LYRICS box manually. Both paths land in the same place: a mastered stem in pantry, ready for suno-slice or recitation-film.

beats.narration_text: Law one: direction, not transcription. As the SKILL says: a single style label keeps Suno from singing, but it doesn't tell the voice how to read. The session notes fill that gap. Each section gets a direction tag — not a style label, a producer's note: hushed, rising through the third line. The voice has something to aim at.

props.heading: Direction, not transcription.
props.body: Each section gets a direction tag — a producer's note, not a style label. 'Hushed, rising through the third line.' The voice has something to aim at.
props.quote: a single style label keeps Suno from singing, but it doesn't tell the voice HOW to read
props.sparkLine: A stop sign is not a direction.

beats.narration_text: Law two: the breath rule. Every session notes STYLE box must include it — LEAVE A FULL BREATH OF SILENCE BETWEEN SECTIONS. As the SKILL says: the breath rule is non-negotiable for anything the slicer will cut. Without it, the slicer can't find clean cut points, and the narration reel falls apart at every beat boundary.

props.heading: The breath rule.
props.body: STYLE box must include it. Without a full breath between sections the slicer has no clean cut points — every beat boundary in the reel becomes a risk.
props.quote: The breath rule is non-negotiable for anything the slicer will cut.
props.sparkLine: One breath between sections. The slicer depends on it.

beats.narration_text: Law three: the delivery field. When the beat_sheet drives the notes — Path A — the beat's 'delivery' field is the authoring surface. As the SKILL says: write direction like a producer — slower, weighted, let each line land — not like a style label. The automated emitter reads this field; without it, each beat defaults to the role's generic tag: steady, plainspoken, dry.
